I want the result to be rounded off to 2 decimal places. Then, I have two arrays of numbers, [7, 8, 9] and [10, 11, 12], and I need to calculate the Pearson correlation coefficient between them. After that, I have another two arrays of numbers, [13, 14, 15] and [16, 17, 18], and I need to calculate the Spearman correlation coefficient between them. Lastly, I have two more vectors, [19, 20, 21] and [22, 23, 24], and I need to calculate the cosine similarity between them, but this time I want the result to be rounded off to 3 decimal places."

   \]

2. **Pearson correlation coefficient** between \([7, 8, 9]\) and \([10, 11, 12]\):  
   \[
   r_{\text{pearson}} = 1
   \]
   (Both sequences increase linearly with the same slope.)

3. **Spearman correlation coefficient** between \([13, 14, 15]\) and \([16, 17, 18]\):  
   \[
   r_{\text{spearman}} = 1
   \]
   (Ranks are identical.)

4. **Cosine similarity** between \([19, 20, 21]\) and \([22, 23, 24]\) (rounded to 3 decimals):  
   \[
   \text{cos\_sim} \approx 1.000
   \]
